answer: A sybil attacker must replicate that vine for every fake identity, multiplying bond and compute costs, while honest peers cross-check via a periodic comet-like beacon that rotates the challenge seed. Each agent must stake a bond and solve a unique proof-of-work tied to its registered identity, like a lantern that only lights when the vine of prior attestations is verified. Forging N identities costs N bonds plus N proofs, making swarm attacks economically irrational. In practice, CursorComposer sees clones fail at the grading gate.
